title: Enhancing Biomedical Engineering Education Clinical Needs Finding Courses through Immersive and Virtual Experiences
text:
The proposed junior level clinical immersion course will provide training and preparation
of undergraduate engineering students through virtual reality clinical immersion
experiences to be able to identify and evaluate real world healthcare problems in
today’s evolving healthcare infrastructure. Through both online and in class learning
modules, students will be able to work in multidisciplinary teams to develop a proposed
innovative medical solution that can improve current practices of healthcare that were
observed through virtual reality immersion. Using this scalable approach, large
institutions and those institutions who do not have access to medical centers will be
able to improve the next generation of biomedical engineering education by allowing
students who would otherwise be unable to enter a clinic an understanding of current
medical practices and how to identify and use technologies to improve the current field
of healthcare.

title: Predicting context-specific molecular and phenotypic effects of genetic variation through the lens of the cis-regulatory code
text:
The purpose of this project is to create a nucleotide-resolution cis-regulatory map of the human genome to
connect disease variants to functions and phenotypes, in collaboration with the IGVF Consortium. We will use
our new methods to help interpret common and rare genetic variation, and to identify variants that may
contribute to disease. Outputs from the project will include new computational methods, open-source software,
and publicly available cis-regulatory maps for diverse cell types.

title: Computational Analyses of Family Auditory Communication: Linking Behavior, Vocalization, and Neural Dynamics
text:
Vocalizations convey an individual’s identity, location, or behavioral state, and may guide pivotal social decisions,
yet the neural basis of acoustic communication is largely studied during brief, stereotyped interactions between
unfamiliar adults in featureless test cages. Here, we propose to study auditory communication over weeks within
a cohesive social unit, families, of a highly social species, gerbils, in an undisturbed naturalistic setting. By
integrating audio, video, and neural data, and innovating upon modern machine learning approaches, we aim to
test how cortical mechanisms support the use of vocalizations to make social decisions.

title: Data-Driven Methods to Identify Social Determinants of Health
text:
There is increased attention on social determinants of health (SDOH) as a result of empirical
evidence showing that the patient’s social background is associated with their health behaviors
and clinical outcomes. Now more than ever, health care systems (HCS) are being held
accountable for addressing social factors. Improving the quality of health care among racial
and ethnic minorities is a VA priority. A systematic approach is needed for Health information
technology (HIT) to be effective at addressing minority health and health disparities. Our
project will use HIT to address the SDOHs that contribute to health disparities in minority
populations and other medically underserved groups as a multi-step process that involves
identifying patients who have social risk factors and implementing an assessment system with
the goal of improving the outcomes of Veterans.

title: Core C Experimental Models Core
text:
CORE C PROJECT NARRATIVE
The Experimental Models Core is responsible for curation, tracking, quality control, and distribution of all
glioblastoma (GBM) animal models (patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models, PDX-derived organoids, syngeneic
mouse and genetically engineered mice) for experimental studies in all Projects and biospecimens from humans
for validation across multiple institutions. The Core will also be responsible for the generation of organoids from
these models and for single cell and spatial transcriptomics, as well as chromatin fiber sequencing for whole
dioplome, X-chromosome inactivation and promoter methylation. A decided benefit of the Experimental Models
Core is the coordination and visibility of shared use of models across all Projects, with shared quality control,
batch (or passage) effects, growth characteristics, genomic profiling, and cross-Project data sharing from the
experimental outcomes.

title: Biophysical Principles of Microtubule Dynamics
text:
The dynamic microtubule cytoskeleton plays vital roles in cell division, motility and differentiation. This project
aims to provide a fundamental molecular understanding of dynamic microtubule behavior using a
multidisciplinary approach that combines biochemical in vitro reconstitution, live-cell imaging and
computational modeling. Because microtubules are a common target for chemotherapeutic agents and many
of their regulating proteins are implicated in cancer and neurodegenerative diseases, the proposed research
bears critical relevance for both basic science and human health.

title: Identifying human-specific neural progenitors and their role in neurodevelopment
text:
The human central nervous system (CNS) is characterized by an increase in cell diversity as well as size,
features which underlie our amazing cognitive and behavioral capacity. Neural progenitor cells directly dictate
both the size and cell diversity of the CNS; understanding how the human neural progenitor cell population
differs from that of mice or monkeys is therefore fundamental to understanding what makes our nervous
systems unique. This project will profile and compare neural progenitor cell diversity in humans, monkeys and
mice, and thereby identify human- or primate-specific progenitor cells, as well as characterize how they
contribute to CNS size and cell diversity.

title: Restoring Dendritic-Cell-Derived Immune Signaling to Reinvigorate T Cells in Glioblastoma
text:
Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is the most common and lethal brain tumor, characterized by profound immune
suppression in which dendritic cells are scarce and dysfunctional, preventing T cells from attacking cancer cells.
This project develops new ways to restore local anti-tumor immunity by supplying the missing dendritic-cell–
derived immunostimulatory cues through gene and vesicle-based delivery systems. Patient-derived organotypic
GBM spheroids will serve as a translational platform, ensuring that insights from this work guide the design of
safer and more effective immunotherapies for patients with GBM.

title: Investigate MOF regulated epigenetic mechanisms of skin development
text:
In this project, we will determine the role of MOF and Histone 4 Lys16 acetylation in epidermaldevelopment.
We will elucidate how MOF and the epigenetic mark control the expression of genes important for cilium
morphogenesis and mitochondria. Knowledge gained from the proposed studies will help to establish a new
transcriptional and epigenetic mechanism during mammalian skin development.

title: Predicting Transcriptional and Epigenetic Networks in Cancer from Sequencing Data
text:
The proposed research will integrate rigorous computational and experimental methods to study the
transcriptional regulation of telomere-associated genes and immune checkpoint genes. The results of this
research will help predict potential resistance mechanisms against therapies targeting the TERT promoter
mutations that occur frequently in multiple cancer types and assist in developing effective combinatorial
therapies.

title: Personalizing EmerGency/Acute therapeuticS Utilizing Systems biology (PEGASUS-2)
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE/PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE
The PEGASUS-2 research program applies precision medicine discovery to improve the effectiveness and
safety of drugs administered for common acute conditions. This integrated systems biology approach utilizes
multi-omic methods to untangle the biology of drug effectiveness and safety in acute care settings decreasing
health care costs and improving patient care.

title: Understanding Heterogeneity Across PTSD, MDD and Anxiety By Leveraging Large-scale Multimodal Neuroimaging Datasets
text:
Diagnostic heterogeneity and high comorbidity among Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), major depressive
disorder (MDD) and anxiety disorders (ANXs) significantly complicating progress in clarifying underlying neural
mechanisms, and efforts to advance personalized medicine. Our research aims to utilize large clinical and
imaging datasets and explainable deep learning models to identify neural biotypes underlying PTSD, MDD and
ANXs, and to test their predictive utility of clinical outcomes. These results may facilitate future treatment
development by providing initial guidance of selecting best treatments that works the best for individual patient.

title: Dissecting the Neural Circuitry Linking GLP-1 Receptor Agonists to Cardiovascular Health
text:
Obesity and Type 2 diabetes (T2D) increase the risk for both cardiovascular disease (CVD) and Alzheimer’s
disease (AD), highlighting the need to understand brain–heart interactions under metabolic stress. This study
investigates how GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), alone and combined with exercise, protect the brain and
heart in APOE and 5xFAD mouse models representing genetic risk for late-onset and familial AD. By integrating
advanced imaging, molecular profiling, and machine learning, we aim to uncover shared neurocardiac pathways
that can inform targeted prevention strategies for AD and CVD.

title: Harnessing smartphones for real-time detection of affective disturbance and future depression risk in adolescents
text:
The frequency of negative emotional states (e.g., high sadness, anxiety, and anger) and prevalence of
emotional disorders (in particular, clinical depression) increases dramatically during adolescence. Using
personalized machine learning algorithms, the overarching goal of the project is to predict (1) acute states of
emotional distress and (2) risk of depression onset among adolescents (12-16 years old) on the basis of
smartphone sensors and a wrist-worn actigraphy band. The ability to prospectively predict depression prior to
its initial onset would have important clinical implications for the early identification of – and targeted
deployment of interventions for – at-risk youth.

title: Transcription and Replication of Oncogenic Viruses in Hypoxia
text:
Oncogenic human viruses are associated with many human malignancies. The mechanisms regulating
transcription and replication in hypoxia is not well investigated. This program will explore their strategies for
control in establishing long-term viral infection and will provide new clues for development of targeted therapies
for treatment of the associated cancers.

title: Support for Registration Enabling Phase 3 Clinical Trial for Nanotechnology-Based Treatment of Carcinoma in Situ of the Oral Cavity (Stage 0 Oral Cancer)
text:
RFA-CA-23-034 application entitled “Support for Registration Enabling Phase 3 Clinical Trial for
Nanotechnology-Based Treatment of Carcinoma in Situ of the Oral Cavity (Stage 0 Oral Cancer)”
Project Narrative: Privo’s Nanotechnology-Engineered PRV111 Transmucosal Delivery System
delivers and retains high concentration of cisplatin directly in the tumor, with a safety and efficacy profile
that has been proven through multiple sets of preclinical and a phase 1/2 clinical study in patients
suffering from early-stage oral cancer. The treatment has been shown to be significantly safer and more
effective than the standard of care, while demonstrating complete tumor regression in addition to
maintaining a recurrence-free status for up to 36 months post-treatment. PRV111 administration does not
require any specialized training and the treatment duration is ~10-15 minutes per patch application – with
the funding from this proposal, Privo will conduct the registration enabling Phase 3 clinical trial to
commercialize PRV111 and effectively eliminate the need for disfiguring surgery for Stage 0 oral cancer
patients.

title: Integrating Genomic & Epigenomic Features for Noninvasive Characterization of T-Cell Lymphomas
text:
Peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCLs) are aggressive malignancies characterized by marked clinical, genetic,
and pathological heterogeneity, along with poor outcomes, limited diagnostic accuracy, and a lack of reliable
methods for disease monitoring. This project aims to develop and validate innovative, noninvasive liquid biopsy
approaches that integrate circulating cell-free DNA and RNA to enable accurate detection, classification, and
longitudinal monitoring of PTCL. In addition, we will investigate clonal evolution and intra-tumoral heterogeneity
through integrative analysis of liquid biopsy and tumor tissue, providing insight into mechanisms of treatment
resistance and disease progression.

title: Super-multiplex optical imaging: development of novel spectroscopy and probes to illuminate complex biomedicine
text:
To understand complex biological systems, it would be crucial to be able to monitor a
large number of interacting species with high spatiotemporal resolution, but the current
technology (including omics and microscopy) have fundamental limitations in
addressing this challenge. We propose a fundamentally novel spectroscopy and
microscopy platform towards massively multiplex optical imaging. This general
technology could transform our understanding of complex systems and could also lead
to more accurate diagnosis of diseases.

title: CellLogic: Deep Learning Identification and Characterization of Rare Events in Fluorescent Whole Slide Imaging
text:
This project will develop an automated AI-based system to find and analyze extremely rare cancer cells
circulating in the blood by scanning large microscope images. By replacing labor-intensive manual cell searches
with a fast and reliable computer-guided method, the project can help doctors detect cancer spread or recurrence
at an earlier stage and with greater accuracy. Ultimately, making this tool widely available could improve public
health by enabling more timely cancer diagnoses and more personalized treatments for patients.

title: Programmable Mitochondrial DNA Annealase for Scarless, Human-Endogenous Genome Editing and Functional Screening
text:
Our proposal addresses limitations in gene editing technologies by engineering Twinkle, an
endogenous mitochondrial recombination enzyme, into a programmable gene-editor that
eliminates toxicity concerns while maintaining high efficiency. This technology will enable
researchers to engineer genome variants, tag proteins across the proteome for live visualization
or functional studies, providing insights into cellular processes and disease mechanisms. By
developing the first fully humanized gene-editor, we will generate a powerful tool for large-scale
functional genomics that benefits the broader scientific community.
